headline: Yields still bite, but risk appetite stabilizes into Trump-Xi summit
body: Futures are modestly higher heading into Friday — S&P 500 futures up about 0.3%, Nasdaq-100 futures up roughly 0.5%, Dow futures adding around 120 points — a tentative bounce after a week dominated by the bond market rather than earnings or growth data. The 10-year Treasury yield touched roughly 5.23% on Thursday, its highest since 2007, with the 30-year near 5.5%, as another Fed official pushed the case for a further hike following the FOMC's 25-basis-point move earlier this month. The pressure has hit the rate-sensitive Dow hardest, on pace for a fourth straight losing week, while the S&P and a Nasdaq led by AI and mega-cap names are both still positive week-to-date — a split that reads less as broad risk-off and more as rotation away from duration-sensitive, cyclical exposure.

Crude has been the other swing factor: Brent eased roughly 0.9% to around $106 a barrel, pulling back from a $108 high, as U.S.-Iran talks in New York raised hopes for a truce and a wider reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, even as Houthi strikes on Saudi energy infrastructure kept a floor under prices. Alongside that, the Trump-Xi summit produced concrete, market-friendly headlines — an extended trade truce and a newly announced U.S.-China AI dialogue — removing one more overhang heading into the weekend. Retail chatter stayed concentrated rather than frothy: social trackers show attention clustered on AI-adjacent mega-caps (Nvidia, Meta, Micron) alongside a familiar pop in meme names like GameStop, so today's read leans more on rates and diplomacy than on any organized shift in positioning.
